# First-Class Functions

> **Gap** GAP-FUNCTIONS-001

[Functions are first-class values and can be assigned, passed, and returned](#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-2):

```metel
fun add(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    return a + b;
}

fun apply(f: |i64| -> i64, x: i64) -> i64 {
    return f(x);
}

fun main() -> i64 {
    let f := add;
    let inc := |x: i64| -> i64 { return x + 1; };
    return f(1, 2) + apply(inc, 4);
}
```

The type of a function or closure is written as `|ParamTypes| -> ReturnType`. `->` and the return type are always present
in a written function type.

A named function declared with its own `<T>` generics (`fun identity<T>(x: T) -> T
{ ... }`) may always be called directly (`identity(3)`, `identity::<i64>(3)`).

A generic named function may be bound with a bare, unannotated `let`; the binding stays
polymorphic, so its later uses may each instantiate it differently (`let alias = identity;
alias(3); alias("x");`). It may also be passed as a higher-order argument when the receiving
parameter position is concrete — for example, `apply(identity, 3)` when `apply`'s parameter
is `|i64| -> i64`, not itself generic.

Referencing it in a position where nothing pins down a concrete instantiation —
a parameter position that is itself still generic in the callee (rank-2), or an
expression position with no expected type and no enclosing `let` — is still
`T0003`. There is also no standalone instantiation-without-calling value form:
`identity::<i64>` not immediately followed by a call is a parse error, not a
type error — see [Turbofish](calls.md#spec.functions.turbofish.legality-3).

A written function type (`|T| -> U`) is [move-only for its by-value use](#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-3),
at every nesting depth: a function value may be called through it any number of
times, but using it by value twice — `let a := f; let b := f;` — is a
use-after-move, even when the underlying value (a named function, or a closure
whose captures are all `Copy`) is itself copyable ([Closures](closures/capture-semantics.md#spec.functions.closures.legality-20)).

Copyability doesn't survive the written type: it's [erased the moment such a value
flows into a slot whose written type is a function type](#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-4) —
a `let` / `var` binding, an ascription, an argument, or a return — and isn't
recovered further downstream. A bare generic type parameter is not a written
function type and keeps the resolved value's own capability.

`copy |T| -> U` is the written spelling of a copyable function type ([rules](#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-5)): its values may be duplicated by value, and only a function value proved copyable is accepted into it.

> **Gap** GAP-FUNCTIONS-003

> **Gap** GAP-FUNCTIONS-002

<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-1}

Function and closure types use `|ParameterTypes| -> ReturnType`; `->` and the
return type are always written. Neither `(ParameterTypes) -> ReturnType` nor
`fun(ParameterTypes) -> ReturnType` is a function-type syntax.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-2}

A non-generic named function and a closure are values of their function type and may be
bound, passed as arguments, and returned as results. A generic named function (declared
with its own `<T>` generics) may be called directly, bound with a bare unannotated `let`
(staying polymorphic across that binding's own later uses), or passed as a higher-order
argument whose receiving parameter position is itself concrete. Referencing it anywhere
else that doesn't pin down a concrete instantiation — including a parameter position
that is itself still generic in the callee — is `T0003`.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 25e71d8966dfb6e54799ec22be9247609654a833 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-3}

A written function type (`|T| -> U`) has move-only by-value use-multiplicity at
every nesting depth, matching exactly against a copyable one: a value of it may
be called (subject to `once` / `var`) and moved, but not duplicated by value. A
bare generic parameter is not a written function type.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-4}

A function value the compiler proved copyable is accepted into a written
function-type slot by moving; the slot's copyability is not carried by the
written type and is not recoverable downstream.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 0f4973466a31348e95cf0bc600ea88d4e8bc849a -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-5}

`copy` is a qualifier on a written function type, written in the same prefix position as `once` and `var` and in any order with them: `copy |T| -> U`, `copy once |T| -> U`, `copy var |T| -> U`. It is contextual: it is a qualifier only before a function type, a class keyword only before `struct`, `enum` or `record` ([declaration clauses](../declarations/aspects/declaration-clauses.md#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-6)), and an ordinary identifier elsewhere.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-6}

A slot of type `copy |T| -> U` accepts a function value only if the compiler proves it copyable from its captures ([closures](closures/capture-semantics.md#spec.functions.closures.legality-20)): a named function, a closure with no captures, or a closure whose captures are all `Copy`. A closure that owns a capture that is not `Copy`, or that holds an exclusive reference `[&var x]` (which is not `Copy`), is a type mismatch (`T0001`) whose message says that a function value is copyable only if it is a named function or a closure whose captures are all `Copy`.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-7}

A value of type `copy |T| -> U` may be duplicated by value (`let a := f; let b := f;`); a value of a bare written function type may not ([legality-3](#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-3)). A `copy |T| -> U` value flows into a bare `|T| -> U` slot, and a copyable value into either, by moving ([legality-4](#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-4)); a bare value is not accepted where `copy` is required (`T0001`). Below the first function level (a callback that takes a callback) the qualifier matches exactly, as `once` and `var` do.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-8}

`copy` in the prefix of a closure literal (`[x] copy |y| ...`) is a parse error (`P0001`): a literal's copyability is derived from its captures, not asserted.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-9}

A value of type `copy |T| -> U` satisfies `Copy` and, by the entailment of `Copy`, `Clone`, through the aspect resolver, the answer move checking gets ([Copy](../ownership/copy.md#spec.ownership.copy.legality-3)): one property with two spellings, `copy struct` and `copy |T| -> U`. It is `Discard` once the `Discard` check exists; until then every type is `Discard` and nothing is checked.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.legality-10}

`copy var |T| -> U` is a copyable function whose call mutates its own captured state. Each copy owns an independent copy of that state, so copies diverge as they are called. A `[&var x]` capture, which aliases state the closure does not own, is not `Copy` and so cannot be `copy` (legality-6).

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 58b51abc04d9a96abb3604f28b34f09b66dcaa36 -->

##### Dynamic Semantics Rule {#spec.functions.first-class-functions.dynamics-1}

Copying a `copy |T| -> U` value duplicates its environment. Every capture is `Copy`, so this is a representation copy that runs no user code ([Copy](../ownership/copy.md#spec.ownership.copy.legality-3)).

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8c6d0f7b3ee655a60d0b4ad455c98950fe4cc311 -->
